$comment: Documented exceptions for the `audit` CI job (scripts/audit-check.mjs).
Every entry MUST carry: an `advisory` (GHSA id) or a `package` scope, a `reason`,
an `approvedBy`, and an `expires` date (YYYY-MM-DD). An entry without `expires`,
or past its `expires` date, does not waive anything AND fails the job — an expired
waiver forces a re-review instead of letting accepted risk become permanent.
Prefer advisory-scoped entries. Package-scoped entries are used below only where a
single upstream version bump resolves a whole cluster of advisories at once, and
enumerating 30+ ids would imply a per-advisory review that did not happen.
Baseline recorded 2026-08-14 during the P0-adapted slice: npm audit reported
14 vulnerabilities (2 low, 11 high, 1 critical) against the dependency set pinned
in package.json at that time.
Updated 2026-08-14 by the dependency-security slice: next 14.2.0 -> 14.2.35,
eslint-config-next 14.2.0 -> 14.2.35, postcss ^8.4.38 -> ^8.5.26, plus a
non-breaking `npm audit fix`. npm audit now reports 7 vulnerabilities
(2 low, 5 high, 0 critical). The critical Next.js middleware authorization bypass
GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw is CLEARED. Nine waivers were deleted because their advisories
no longer appear: @next/eslint-plugin-next, eslint-config-next,
@typescript-eslint/parser, @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree, brace-expansion,
minimatch, js-yaml, nanoid, and ws.
Updated 2026-09-01 by the issue #67 Next 16 / React 19 / Tailwind 4 migration:
next -> 16.3.4, eslint-config-next in lockstep. This is exactly the remediation
each of the three remaining waivers (next, postcss, glob) named as their own
clearing condition. `npm audit` now reports 0 vulnerabilities at any severity, so
all three are deleted rather than left in place pointing at advisories that no
longer appear.
